item.title: Warriors Withholding Payments To Kristaps Porzingis
item.description:
The Golden State Warriors are withholding payments to Kristaps Porzingis on his $20 million contract indicating that he is not rendering services.

The Warriors are allowed to trade Porzingis at any time before the February 11th trade deadline even without paying him currently. Golden State is exhausting all trade possibilities involving Porzingis.

Porzingis is considering his future in basketball and is out indefinitely. Porzingis began suffering from a prolonged upper respiratory viral illness while with the Boston Celtics in February 2025.

Porzingis was around the Warriors before the start of training camp before he approached Mike Dunleavy Jr. about the condition on the eve of the preseason.

Porzingis is on a two-year, $40 million contract that has only $3 million guaranteed next season.

The Philadelphia 76ers went through a similar situation at the start of the 2021-22 season with Ben Simmons following his trade request.

The Athletic reported that Porzingis and the NBPA are not currently challenging the Warriors' decision to withhold payments.

item.title: Norchad Omier To Sign With Cavs After Agreeing To Two-Way Deal With Wolves
item.description:
Norchad Omier plans to sign a two-way contract with the Cleveland Cavaliers, sources told Michael Scotto of HoopsHype.

Omier originally agreed to sign a two-way deal with the Wolves but changed his mind.

The Wolves now have an open two-way roster spot.

item.title: Chris Boucher Signs With Shanghai Sharks
item.description:
Veteran forward Chris Boucher has signed with the Shanghai Sharks of the Chinese Basketball Association. Boucher is replacing JaVale McGee, who was waived to create the roster spot.

Boucher appeared in nine NBA games with the Boston Celtics last season. He was traded to the Utah Jazz at the trade deadline as the Celtics got under the luxury tax. Utah waived Boucher shortly thereafter.

This is the first overseas foray for the 6-foot-8 forward. Boucher will join former NBA players D'Angelo Russell and Brandon Goodwin as the Sharks three import players.

item.title: Kon Knueppel Leaves Game With Leg Soreness
item.description:
Kon Knueppel left the Charlotte Hornets' 114-104 loss to the Brooklyn Nets on Wednesday night due to leg soreness.

Knueppel, who was making his season debut, lasted six minutes before leaving the game.

Knueppel appeared to reaggravate his left hamstring, with the team calling the injury "soreness in his left leg."

The guard missed all of training camp and preseason with the hamstring injury.

Head coach Charles Lee said Knueppel will be re-evaluated when the team returns to Charlotte.

item.title: Victor Wembanyama After Scoring Career High 52 Points: 'It's Just Figuring Things Out'
item.description:
Victor Wembanyama finished with career highs of 52 points and 24 rebounds as the San Antonio Spurs defeated the Dallas Mavericks 112-111 on Wednesday night.

Wembanyama, who had 29 points and 15 rebounds at halftime, also finished with eight blocks.

"It's just figuring things out," he said. "Sometimes you're one step ahead. Also, I haven't been feeling great lately. I've been sick for a while. And today, I felt like I got my legs back, so it should be more like this more often."

Wembanyama is the second player since blocks became an official stat in 1973-74 with at least 50 points, 20 rebounds, and five blocks in a game.

It was also Wembanyama's second 50-point game for the Spurs.

Dylan Harper added 21 points, with Stephon Castle finishing with 17 points and ten rebounds.

The Spurs were plus-23 with Wembanyama on the court and minus-22 with the center off the court.

Kyrie Irving, who lead the Mavs with 29 points, missed a go-ahead jumper with three seconds left in the game.

item.title: Vit Krejci Suffers Fractured Lower Leg
item.description:
Vit Krejci suffered a fractured lower leg against the Phoenix Suns on Wednesday night, according to Portland Trail Blazers head coach Micah Nori.

Krejci suffered the injury in the third quarter when attempting to take a charge from Miles Bridges.

Krejci is averaging 2.7 points and 1.6 rebounds on the year.

item.title: Center Cherif Millogo Commits To Kentucky
item.description:
7-foot-5 center Cherif Millogo announced his commitment to Kentucky for the class of 2027 on Thursday.

Millogo, who is ranked No. 8 in his class, is head coach Mark Pope's highest-ranked recruit in his time at Kentucky.

Former NBA player Luc Mbah a Moute is Millogo's legal guardian.

Millogo joins No. 31 ranked prospect Ryan Hampton in Kentucky's 2027 class.

item.title: Kristaps Porzingis Motivated To Agree To Contract Buyout If Traded
item.description:
Kristaps Porzingis would have strong interest in negotiating a contract buyout that allows him to officially walk away from basketball and get some of the money on his $20 million deal that the Golden State Warriors are currently withholding, three sources tell Jake Fischer of The Stein Line. Porzingis has only $3 million guaranteed on his contract for the 2027-28 season.

The Warriors do not consider Porzingis' absence to be excused, which is why they are witholding payments to the big man.

Porzingis is contemplating retirement from the NBA as he continues to deal with "health stuff that you can't exactly pinpoint."

The Warriors are actively shopping Porzingis on the trade market and are motivated to move him in exchange for a player that can help this season. Golden State expected Porzingis to play in at least half of their games this season until he had a recurrence of his health issue in September that forced him back to the sidelines.

The Warriors were in a similar position during the early part of the 2024-25 season when De'Anthony Melton tore his ACL. The Warriors ended up trading him to the Brooklyn Nets for Dennis Schroder and eventually included Schroder for Jimmy Butler.
